Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

soft adjective

to the touch

also softer

classical

Plin. NH 15.82: fīcīs mollis omnibus tāctus
Ov. Ars 1.475: quid mollius undā?
Traupman 382

mollis, molle

adjective, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Soft to touch, to sit or lie on, to eat; the opposite is dūrus (see hard). A soft voice is summissa vōx (see in a low voice).

Other words

  • tener, tenera, tenerum — tender, soft (of young things and of food)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 45.1: terra tenera (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 123.2: tenerum et silīgineum, of bread · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • fīcīs mollis omnibus tāctus, mātūrīs frūmenta intus

    all figs are soft to the touch; ripe ones have seeds insidePlin. NH 15.82

  • alicam in aquam īnfunditō. ubi bene mollis erit, in mortārium pūrum inditō

    Put the groats in water. When they are nice and soft, put them in a clean mortar.Cato Agr. 76

See also hard, in a low voice, gentle, soft-boiled egg.
